title: Deep Learning Foundations
purpose: A complete ten-unit mathematical and computational foundation in deep learning, with original derivations, substantial problem sheets, reproducible small numerical investigations and an evidence-led cumulative project.
description:
This course connects the mathematics of neural networks with the evidence needed to interpret their results. Ten fully authored units cover tensors and evaluation discipline; gradients and backpropagation; MLPs; deep linear learning dynamics; optimisation; generalisation and early stopping; regularisation; convolution; attention and sequences; and representation learning with a cumulative project.

Neuromatch Academy Deep Learning provides the reading spine (content CC BY 4.0; code BSD-3-Clause). Corniversity supplies original explanations and exercises, deriving conditions rather than treating every tutorial simplification as a general theorem. Exact tutorial text was read for the new units on 2026-11-12; embedded videos were not watched. These rolling pages are source snapshots, not a claim to teach the latest frontier systems.

Each unit has a lesson, progressive hints, weighted rubrics and complete instructor reasoning. Computational reference solutions contain executable standard-library Python and observed author-run output. The final CPU-only project trains a small tanh network from scratch, fits preprocessing and PCA only on training inputs, selects checkpoints/configuration on validation across all declared seeds, and reports untouched test/shift results, baselines and actual failures. No external training service, pretrained download or billed generation is needed.

Prepared content is distinct from independent academic review and from learner mastery. Source and solution reviews are tracked separately; the course makes no accreditation, state-of-the-art or real-world performance claim from its synthetic experiments.

outcomes.description: Derive and analyse gradient descent and backpropagation: step-size conditions and rates on quadratics, the descent lemma for smooth functions, and gradients through a computational graph by the chain rule, by hand and in code.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Hand derivations with numerical checks, a step-size analysis with the divergence threshold proved, and an explanation of reverse- versus forward-mode cost.

outcomes.description: Apply the evidence discipline: separate train, validation and test data, identify leakage in a described pipeline, compare against baselines, and quantify the uncertainty of a reported metric.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: A leakage audit that names each leak and explains why the reported metric is not evidence; a calculation of the sampling error of an accuracy estimate; notebooks that report splits, baselines and seeds.

outcomes.description: Explain overfitting and generalisation in overparameterised networks and use early stopping, L1/L2 penalties, dropout and augmentation with their trade-offs stated.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Learning-curve interpretation, regularisation experiments with validation-based selection, and a written account of what each regulariser changes in the optimisation problem.

outcomes.description: Derive convolution as a linear operator under specified boundary rules and attention as content-dependent weighting (linear in values only with weights fixed); compute shapes/costs, prove relevant symmetry statements and justify architecture assumptions.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Operator/adjoint proofs and gradient checks, counterexamples to blanket pooling invariance, masked-attention calculations and a permutation-symmetry argument.

outcomes.description: Produce a reproducible computational notebook that trains a model, reports a baseline, states the split and seed policy, examines failure cases and explains the model's behaviour.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: The final project notebook and its written explanation, assessed against the department's reporting conventions.

outcomes.description: Analyse reconstruction and contrastive representation objectives and evaluate what a representation preserves for a downstream task.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: PCA label-information counterexample, ELBO/contrastive derivations and a train-only representation ablation with limits stated.

assessmentSpecs.title: Problem sets and notebooks
assessmentSpecs.description: Each unit's exercises (derivations, calculations, short code) are submitted as immutable attempts and assessed with line-localised feedback. Every notebook states its data split, baseline and seed policy; a notebook without them is returned unassessed.
rubricSummary: split, baseline and seed policy stated
code read and explained, not only run

assessmentSpecs.title: Evidence audit
assessmentSpecs.description: After unit 6: a written audit of one described or published training pipeline (a labelled synthetic case is provided if none is chosen), identifying leakage, baseline and variance problems and stating what the reported metric does and does not show. Open book, untimed by default.
rubricSummary: every leak named with its mechanism
claims limited to what the evidence supports

assessmentSpecs.title: Final project: train, break and explain
assessmentSpecs.description: The complete unit10 train/break/explain study: implement and gradient-check a small CPU model; preserve independent partitions and training-only transforms; select checkpoints/configuration on validation across all declared seeds; evaluate fixed baselines, final and shifted data; report actual failures and representation/architecture assumptions. Runnable script or notebook plus an annotated report.
rubricSummary: baselines, uncertainty limits and actual failures

provenance.authoringMethod: Inherited units1–2 retained; units3–10 directly authored in Codex after reading actual Neuromatch tutorial text, with original proofs, counterexamples and exercises. Complete reference programs were executed locally on CPU using only the Python standard library. No Corniversity provider generation, subscription credits, external training jobs or pretrained weights were used.
reviewerNotes: All ten units contain full lessons and assessed work; academic review is tracked separately from availability.
New source snapshot URLs/hashes and topic map are recorded in source-review-manifest.json and REVIEW.md; embedded videos were not watched.

Corrected source simplifications include dot product versus cosine, conditional SVD decoupling, second moment versus variance, pooling invariance, adaptive weight decay and full attention nonlinearity.
Complete executable reference code/results are in the instructor material; the final project also has standalone files in labs/.
Fixed synthetic output verifies a particular numerical run, not learner-tested effectiveness or external performance.

Final independent academic review completed 2026-11-12: SCIENCE_REVIEW.md plus LEAD_ACADEMIC_REVIEW.md, with source-specific scope and limitations. Every current exercise has independently checked reference reasoning. Not human certification or measured learning effectiveness.

externalSyllabusNote: Adapted study path using Neuromatch Academy Deep Learning materials (content CC BY 4.0; code BSD-3-Clause). The original course is a three-week intensive (days W1D1–W3D5 with pods, daily projects and a final presentation). Corniversity re-paces W1D1–W3D3 as ten units over an evening-study term, writes its own lessons and exercises, and omits the pod, project-time and Colab workflow. This is not a Neuromatch course and confers no certificate from Neuromatch.
